# pbs_datastore_status (Data Source)

Reads how full a Proxmox Backup Server datastore is: the size, use and free space of the file system it is on, as the dashboard of the web interface shows them, and when PBS expects it to be full. The figures need `Datastore.Audit` or `Datastore.Backup` on the datastore; with a privilege on one of its namespaces only, they are null.

A removable datastore that is not mounted has no figures either, and a datastore PBS cannot open — in maintenance mode `offline`, say — has `error` instead; reading such a datastore is not an error.

For a datastore on S3, `s3_statistics` has the requests PBS made to its bucket and the bytes it moved; with `count_backups`, `counts` has how many backup groups and snapshots the datastore holds. PBS answers them in one more call, which, like the figures, needs `Datastore.Audit` or `Datastore.Backup` on the datastore.

PBS answers with the figures of every datastore of the server at once, and opens each for them, but removable ones that are not mounted. Opening a datastore takes the lock of PBS's datastore configuration, which a task such as an S3 refresh can hold for minutes. PBS then waits 10 seconds for the lock for each datastore, so the read can outlast the provider's `request_timeout`, and has its refusal for the lock as the `error` of each datastore, with a warning — or, with privileges on its namespaces only, leaves the datastore out.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "pbs_datastore_status" "store1" {
  store = "store1"
}

output "store1_free_gib" {
  value = floor(data.pbs_datastore_status.store1.avail / 1073741824)
}

# A warning in every plan once the datastore's file system is more than 90 %
# full.
check "store1_space" {
  assert {
    condition     = data.pbs_datastore_status.store1.used < 0.9 * data.pbs_datastore_status.store1.total
    error_message = "The file system of datastore store1 is more than 90 % full."
  }
}

# How many backups the datastore holds. PBS goes through the whole datastore
# to count them, so it does so only when asked.
data "pbs_datastore_status" "store1_backups" {
  store         = "store1"
  count_backups = true
}

locals {
  store1_counts = data.pbs_datastore_status.store1_backups.counts
}

output "store1_snapshots" {
  value = local.store1_counts.vm.snapshots + local.store1_counts.ct.snapshots + local.store1_counts.host.snapshots
}

# A warning in every plan once a datastore on S3 has made 1.6 million PUT
# requests to its bucket since its counters were last reset.
# s3_statistics is null on a file system and before PBS 4.1.7, which try
# turns into 0.
data "pbs_datastore_status" "s3store1" {
  store = "s3store1"
}

check "s3store1_requests" {
  assert {
    condition     = try(data.pbs_datastore_status.s3store1.s3_statistics.put, 0) < 1600000
    error_message = "Datastore s3store1 has made 1.6 million PUT requests to its bucket since its counters were reset."
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `store` (String) Name of the datastore, such as `store1`.

### Optional

- `count_backups` (Boolean) Whether to count the backup groups and snapshots of the datastore, for `counts`. PBS then goes through every namespace, backup group and snapshot of the datastore on disk — in its local cache for a datastore on S3, without requests to the bucket — before it answers, which takes the longer the more backups the datastore holds. The provider's `request_timeout` bounds that wait: a datastore with very many snapshots may need a longer one. The datastore's summary in the web interface, while open, counts them every five seconds. Defaults to `false`, which leaves `counts` null.

### Read-Only

- `avail` (Number) Bytes free for the datastore on that file system.
- `backend_type` (String) Where the datastore keeps its chunks: `filesystem` or `s3`. PBS reports it with the figures from 4.1.6; on older releases, the provider reads it from the datastore's configuration, which needs `Datastore.Audit` on the datastore, and it is null without that.
- `counts` (Attributes) How many backup groups, and snapshots in them, the datastore holds in all its namespaces, by backup type, as the datastore's summary in the web interface shows them. Groups without snapshots are not counted, and a snapshot still being written is. With `Datastore.Backup` but not `Datastore.Audit` on the datastore, PBS counts, outside namespaces where the provider has `Datastore.Audit` or `Datastore.Read`, only the groups it owns: a user's own and its API tokens', an API token's own. A group or snapshot removed while PBS counts — by a prune, a sync or the deletion of a namespace — fails the read, which a `check` block turns into a warning. Null without `count_backups`, and when the figures are null. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--counts))
- `error` (String) Why PBS could not open the datastore, such as its refusal for the lock of its datastore configuration while a task holds it; null when it could.
- `estimated_full_date` (Number) When PBS expects the datastore to be full, in seconds since the Unix epoch, from the trend of its use over the last month: `0` when its use does not change, and a time in the past when it shrinks. Null until PBS has seven half-hour samples of its use, a few hours after it starts tracking the datastore; early estimates are rough.
- `mount_status` (String) Whether a removable datastore is mounted: `mounted` or `notmounted`; `nonremovable` for any other datastore.
- `s3_statistics` (Attributes) For a datastore on S3, the requests PBS has made to its bucket and the bytes it has moved since the counters were last reset — by `counter_reset_schedule` of `pbs_datastore`, or with `proxmox-backup-manager s3 endpoint reset-counters` — as the datastore's summary in the web interface shows them: the counters `notification_thresholds` compares with its thresholds. They include the requests of creating the datastore, and those of `pbs_s3_endpoint_check` with the datastore's name as `store_prefix`. PBS counts a request once however often it retries it, whatever the object store answers, and keeps the counters on disk across restarts, also for a datastore deleted and created again with the same name, endpoint and bucket. Null for a datastore on a file system, on PBS before 4.1.7, and when the figures are null. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--s3_statistics))
- `total` (Number) Size of the file system the datastore is on, in bytes; for a datastore on S3, that of its local cache.
- `used` (Number) Bytes in use on that file system, by the datastore and anything else on it. Pruned backups keep their space until garbage collection frees it.

<a id="nestedatt--counts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `counts`

Read-Only:

- `ct` (Attributes) Backups of containers. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--counts--ct))
- `host` (Attributes) Backups of hosts, made with `proxmox-backup-client`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--counts--host))
- `vm` (Attributes) Backups of virtual machines. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--counts--vm))

<a id="nestedatt--counts--ct"></a>
### Nested Schema for `counts.ct`

Read-Only:

- `groups` (Number) Backup groups — one per backup ID in each namespace — with at least one snapshot; `0` when there are none.
- `snapshots` (Number) Snapshots in those groups; `0` when there are none.


<a id="nestedatt--counts--host"></a>
### Nested Schema for `counts.host`

Read-Only:

- `groups` (Number) Backup groups — one per backup ID in each namespace — with at least one snapshot; `0` when there are none.
- `snapshots` (Number) Snapshots in those groups; `0` when there are none.


<a id="nestedatt--counts--vm"></a>
### Nested Schema for `counts.vm`

Read-Only:

- `groups` (Number) Backup groups — one per backup ID in each namespace — with at least one snapshot; `0` when there are none.
- `snapshots` (Number) Snapshots in those groups; `0` when there are none.



<a id="nestedatt--s3_statistics"></a>
### Nested Schema for `s3_statistics`

Read-Only:

- `delete` (Number) `DELETE` requests.
- `downloaded` (Number) Bytes downloaded from the bucket, in the bodies of the answers.
- `get` (Number) `GET` requests, which restores, verification, garbage collection and S3 refreshes make.
- `head` (Number) `HEAD` requests, which checks of objects make.
- `post` (Number) `POST` requests, which garbage collection makes to delete chunks in bulk.
- `put` (Number) `PUT` requests, which backups and syncs make.
- `uploaded` (Number) Bytes uploaded to the bucket, in the bodies of the requests.
